query: How does resolution duration vary across incident category and priority?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Derives a clean category from short_description (connect->connectivity, database, printing->hardware), well grounded. However, the original table already has a 'category' column, so it partially overlaps; still, a normalized/refined category from free text can add leverage for grouping resolution duration. Moderate usefulness given redundancy risk.

per_column.name: incident_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: Individual vs widespread/outage is a meaningful axis distinct from the existing priority field and directly relevant to resolution duration. Grounding is reasonable for clearly-scoped texts (single-user 'Cannot connect' -> individual_access) but 'widespread_impact'/'system_outage' require inference the short_description may not always support, so some values could be over-asserted.

per_column.name: infrastructure_target
per_column.rationale: Well grounded mapping from description to target (WiFi/VPN->network, printing->user_device). But it tracks incident_category very closely (network<->connectivity, database<->database), making it largely a restatement, reducing its independent analytical value for this query.

per_column.name: resolution_complexity_indicator
per_column.rationale: Directly framed around resolution effort, so highly relevant to duration analysis. However labels like 'server_side_failure' vs 'client_side_configuration' are inferred causes the short_description often does not establish (e.g. 'Unable to access online database' -> server_side_failure is an assumption). Meaningful risk of confident specifics beyond evidence.

per_column.name: time_of_incident_context
per_column.rationale: Cleanly derived from opened_at timestamp (18:14->after_hours, 8:50/7:34 near boundary but defensible). A legitimate new axis that could correlate with resolution duration. Well grounded.

per_column.name: repeat_incident_flag
per_column.rationale: A repeat flag is analytically useful for duration. But nothing in the provided per-row source text (short_description, opened_at, closed_by) reliably establishes repetition; the same 'Cannot connect to office VPN' text appears as both True and False, indicating the value is not consistently derivable from stated fields. Weak grounding.

judge.rationale: Most columns give real axes for grouping resolution duration beyond the existing category/priority fields (severity signal, time-of-day, complexity, repeat flag). incident_category and infrastructure_target overlap heavily with each other and with the original category column, lowering their marginal value. Grounding is strong for extraction/time-based columns but weaker for inferred-cause columns (resolution_complexity_indicator, repeat_incident_flag) where labels assert specifics the short text does not clearly support, evidenced by identical source text yielding different repeat flags.
